newsitem.title: USA: CME hog, pork belly futures settle higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hog, pork belly futures settle higher.

text.p: CME hog futures ended higher but gains in nearby months were pared ahead of the close by spreading while back months held most of their gains. Pork belly gains also trimmed but futures finished moderately higher, traders said.

Hog futures finished mostly 0.700 to 0.050 cent per lb higher with February up 0.250 at 75.600 cents. August and October posted new contract highs earlier. Pork bellies ended 1.025 to 0.450 cent higher with February up most at 79.425 cents.
Late spreading of short February and April and long June by traders who still expect weakness in cash markets pared earlier gains in nearbys, traders said.

Futures rallied early when cash markets were not as weak as had been expected and spillover support developed from cattle pits ahead of Friday's Cattle Inventory report. Hog runs and slaughter have not been as large as anticipated which brought on the short covering early, they said.
But pork products remained weak and talk on the trading floor was for lower cash hog prices into early next week. Paring of gains in cattle pits late also weighed on sentiment, they added.
Rand Financials sold late after buying early along with Rosenthal Collins, Lind-Waldock and locals. Smith Barney in Cargill Investor Services bought June late, pit sources said.
In hog options, trading remained quiet with volatility continuing to decline in February on time decay. Volatility was firm in April and beyond, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures showed strength despite a decline in cash belly price quotes at noon. Commercials were rolling short positions back into May while funds were rolling the opposite way and the commercial action prompted local short covering in February, traders said.
Some traders cited the lighter-than-expected pace of hog slaughter for the support.
USDA estimated Thursday's hog slaughter at 349,000 head, bringing the week-to-date total to 1,336,000, below 1,417,000 in the same period a week ago and 1,341,000 a year ago.
R.J. O'Brien, Lind-Waldock and ABN Chicogo Corp bought February and sold back months. Rand was an early seller, pit sources said.
